claims.text: Retention of toughness in L-PBF Al0.5CrCoFeNi is governed by the connectivity of its nano-bridged honeycomb microstructure.
L-PBF Al0.5CrCoFeNi exhibits a nano-bridged honeycomb microstructure comprising an fcc matrix and an interwoven ordered B2 phase.
The ordered B2 phase is concentrated at the solidification-cell boundaries.
Dislocation nano-bridges connect neighboring fcc cells through channels between B2 regions at the cell boundaries.
Cooling rate and thermal gradient control the cellular solidification microstructure and boundary segregation during L-PBF.
Varying cooling rate and thermal gradient can deliberately disrupt or modify B2-network connectivity at cell boundaries.
Relevant L-PBF cooling rates are approximately 10^5–10^7 K/s and thermal gradients are approximately 10^5–10^7 K/m.
A continuous B2 framework promotes formation of dislocation channels connecting the interiors of fcc cells.
The dislocation channels transport dislocations away from a crack tip and thereby promote crack blunting and intrinsic fracture resistance.
Reducing B2-network connectivity makes dislocation transport less effective and causes a loss of toughness.
B2 strengthening, high dislocation density, and solid-solution strengthening contribute to the alloy's strength.
Yield strength will remain comparable to the baseline after B2 connectivity is disrupted because other strengthening mechanisms remain active.
Disrupting B2 connectivity will measurably reduce crack-initiation fracture toughness, KJIc, relative to the baseline.
Standard baseline processing produces an optimized microstructure with well-connected B2 networks.
The mechanism should transfer to additively manufactured high-entropy alloys with similar compositions and processing-induced microstructures.
Cooling-rate changes may introduce microstructural defects that independently influence toughness.
